title: AWS CWI Training in Newark, NJ: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for North Jersey special inspection, bridge, refinery and gas utility welding. Corporate, online or one-to-one formats.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Newark, New Jersey: Six Days for Special Inspection, Bridge, Refinery and Utility Welding Inspectors
html:
North Jersey's welding is dense, varied and heavily regulated: rail bridges on the Northeast Corridor, refinery units along the Arthur Kill, gas mains under city streets, port and airport construction, and building steel that a state-certified special inspector has to sign off. Atlantis NDT prepares Newark-area welders, ironworkers, pipefitters, QC technicians and engineers for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination with a six-day (6-day) course covering Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. There are three ways to take it: corporate (the six days at the employer's facility), online (self-paced, with an instructor answering questions) or one-to-one (sessions with the instructor for a single candidate, online or in person). AWS administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis readies candidates and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Newark, and the company keeps offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. To price a course, send a Newark CWI exam prep enquiry.

The CWI and New Jersey's structural welding special inspector

For many Newark candidates the CWI is tied to a state credential. Under the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, special inspections on Class 1 buildings must be performed by inspectors who are certified in the appropriate specialty, independent of the contractor and responsible to the owner or the owner's agent; the cost falls on the owner, lessee or contractor (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.20). The Department of Community Affairs certifies a Structural Welding Special Inspector to carry out the structural steel welding inspections in the building subcode.

The DCA's special inspector licensing booklet sets four routes to eligibility: four years in a skilled trade directly related to structural steel or welding, an associate degree in a relevant field with two years in that trade, a bachelor's degree with one year, or a current New Jersey engineering license. Candidates must also pass a structural welding special inspector examination, and the booklet accepts either the ICC examination or successful completion of the AWS Certified Welding Inspector examination, or an equivalent the DCA approves. The state certification lasts three years and requires five hours of continuing education per cycle, with licensed professional engineers exempt.

Two practical points follow. Passing the CWI examination can satisfy the examination step for that state certification, but it does not replace the separate DCA application. And the CWI is a personal credential that stays with you, which matters in a market where inspectors move between testing agencies, fabricators and owners. Check the current DCA requirements before you apply, because state rules change.

How the six days work from Newark

The outline is fixed: two days on fundamentals (processes, terms, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, testing, discontinuities, NDT, safety and the arithmetic Part A asks for), one day on Part B measurement and documents, one day working inside the code book you will use for Part C, one day of timed practice papers and one day on weak areas and examination logistics. Day-by-day detail is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

  • Corporate. A special inspection agency, steel fabricator, refinery contractor or utility contractor books the six days for its own people at its own facility. Practice uses its gauges and weld samples and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online. An individual gets a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and sends questions to an instructor as they work. There is no timetable, which helps when your week is set by a turnaround or a site's pour schedule.
  • One-to-one. One candidate takes six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

The practice questions and papers are Atlantis's own, written to the topic areas AWS publishes. None reproduces an AWS examination question, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

What North Jersey welds

Rail and bridge steel: Portal North and the Gateway corridor

Over the Hackensack River near Kearny, NJ TRANSIT and Amtrak have replaced a 116-year-old swing bridge with Portal North, a two-track, high-level, fixed-span bridge that rises 50 feet over the river. The first track entered passenger service in March 2026, with the second track due to move over in the fall. Portal North is a key piece of the Gateway Program, which aims to double rail capacity between Newark and New York, and the corridor will keep generating bridge, tunnel and structural steel work for years. Steel bridge members are typically fabricated under the AWS Bridge Welding Code, D1.5, or under railroad and owner specifications that lean on it, with heavy inspection of main and fracture-critical members.

Refining and petrochemicals along the Arthur Kill

Phillips 66 runs the Bayway refinery in Linden, on the Arthur Kill. Planned turnarounds, such as one that ran into March 2025, bring large crews of pipe welders and boilermakers for short, intense periods. Refinery piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3, with procedures and welders qualified under Section IX, and alloy materials bring preheat, post-weld heat treatment and hardness checks into the inspector's routine. A CWI on a turnaround spends much of each shift on weld maps, welder qualification records and material traceability before any weld goes to the NDT contractor.

Gas mains under the city

PSE&G has been replacing aging gas infrastructure across New Jersey for years. In Newark alone it replaced about 27 miles of cast iron and unprotected steel gas pipe in a project that started in 2020, part of a statewide program to replace hundreds of miles of mains, and the state Board of Public Utilities has approved later phases of that work. Most new distribution mains are plastic, joined by fusion rather than arc welding, but steel pipe remains at regulator stations, larger mains and transmission lines. Steel gas pipeline welding is qualified and accepted under API 1104, which federal pipeline safety rules incorporate, so utility contractors look for inspectors who know that standard.

Port, airport and building construction

Port Newark and the Elizabeth terminals, the airport and a steady flow of downtown, warehouse and institutional buildings keep structural steel moving through the region. Building steel is welded to AWS D1.1, and on larger buildings the structural welding special inspector role described above applies. Warehouse and logistics construction around the port, with its long-span roofs, adds a further stream of fabricator and erector work.

Who hires CWIs around Newark

  • Special inspection agencies and testing laboratories, which need inspectors who hold the CWI and the state Structural Welding Special Inspector certification.
  • Structural fabricators and steel erectors supplying buildings, warehouses and transit projects, who keep CWIs for shop quality control and customer audits.
  • Refinery, chemical and turnaround contractors along the Arthur Kill, who want Section IX and B31.3 fluency.
  • Gas utility and pipeline contractors, who want API 1104 knowledge and comfort with operator qualification paperwork.
  • Bridge and rail fabricators and owners' representatives on corridor work, where D1.5 and owner specifications drive the job.

Across the board, employers here ask which code you know best, whether your welding experience can be verified, and whether you can hold your ground on a rejection with a foreman who is behind schedule.

Choosing the Part C code for New Jersey work

Part C is open book on the one code you choose. Pick the code your work runs on; you will use the book long after the examination is done.

Your North Jersey workBook to considerWhy it fits
Building steel, warehouses, special inspection work, structural fabricationAWS D1.1The structural steel code the building subcode's welding inspections rest on
Bridge and corridor steel for transit and highway ownersAWS D1.5Bridge fabrication, including fracture-critical members
Refinery, chemical plant and power pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification plus process and power piping examination and acceptance
Steel gas mains, stations and transmission pipeAPI 1104Pipeline welder and procedure qualification and acceptance standards
Railcar and locomotive workAWS D15.1Railroad welding for cars and locomotives

Study the edition AWS lists for your examination; it can be older than the one in your office. Background: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, API 1104 and API 1104 acceptance criteria.

The AWS New Jersey Section

The AWS New Jersey Section sits in AWS District 2 and meets in Middlesex, with meetings posted on its site at sections.aws.org; past technical meetings have covered AWS certification and educational resources. For a CWI candidate the section is a useful network: working inspectors and QC managers attend, and they are the people who can confirm your welding history for the AWS application, explain how local agencies use the CWI and the state special inspector certification together, and pass on news of firms that are hiring. AWS members also pay lower AWS examination fees under the fee table published on aws.org.

Where North Jersey welders come from

The region's welders arrive through a mix of union apprenticeships, technical schools and on-the-job training. Ironworker apprenticeships supply much of the structural welding workforce, boilermakers and pipefitters the refinery and plant work. Lincoln Tech's Mahwah and South Plainfield campuses in New Jersey offer a Welding and Fabrication Technology with Pipe program that trains structural and pipe welders. County vocational schools and community colleges add shorter welding courses.

For the CWI, how you learned matters because AWS lets schooling reduce the experience it requires. Completed trade or vocational courses leave four years of welding-related work; a high school diploma alone means five. An associate degree in engineering technology, engineering or physical science sits in the two-year row and a bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology in the one-year row. AWS makes the call on which row a particular program belongs in, so confirm it before you plan around the shorter number. Apprentices should keep their apprenticeship records and journeyman cards; they are among the easiest experience evidence to verify.

Booking the exam from Newark

An approved AWS application produces a confirmation letter with an eligibility code. You use that code to reserve Part A and Part C at a Prometric test center; both are computer-based, and the Prometric site shows the centers nearest Newark. Part B is run by AWS itself at its seminar and examination locations, so check the AWS seminar and exam schedule first, choose a practical date you can reach, and then fit the Prometric bookings into the order and window AWS sets.

Plan for 150 questions on Part A, hands-on tasks with AWS-supplied tools and specimens plus 46 questions on Part B, and roughly 50 to 65 open-book questions on Part C, with at least 72 percent required on each part. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org; the CWI exam budget planner adds up travel, the code book and time away from work.

One local wrinkle: many Newark inspectors also work across the Hudson, where New York City's Department of Buildings sets its own special inspection rules. If that is your market too, read the New York CWI exam prep page.

Studying around turnarounds and construction schedules

Newark-area work runs on several clocks. Refinery turnarounds bring weeks of twelve-hour shifts, often in spring or fall. Construction crews follow steel delivery and pour schedules. Utility crews work long seasons of street openings. The study plan should fit those rhythms rather than fight them.

  1. Cover the fundamentals in a quieter stretch; they are the most reading-heavy part of the outline.
  2. Carry your code book on site and look up the provisions behind the welds you see that week, whether that is D1.1 connection details or B31.3 examination requirements.
  3. Measure real welds with real gauges and record each reading before you judge it; Part B rewards that discipline.
  4. Keep the timed papers for the final weeks before your Prometric appointment, and if a turnaround is coming, book a one-to-one block before or after it so the code work does not stall.

Corporate: six days at a North Jersey employer's site

The corporate format brings the whole six days to one employer's facility for a group of its staff. In the Newark area that might be a special inspection agency preparing several inspectors for the CWI examination ahead of their state applications, a fabricator adding CWIs to its quality plan before a transit package, or a turnaround contractor building inspection depth before the next outage. The practical day uses the company's own fillet, bridge cam, undercut and hi-lo gauges on its own welds, and the code day can split between D1.1, D1.5, API 1104 and the ASME option for a mixed group. Timing can be set around turnarounds and project milestones. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually and must meet the experience and vision requirements personally.

One-to-one, online or in person

For a single candidate, the one-to-one format runs six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It suits an engineer who needs code navigation more than theory, an inspector whose agency needs a CWI on a particular project by a fixed date, or someone retaking one part who wants every session spent on it. The outline is the same as the other formats; only the pace and emphasis change.

Eligibility and vision

Besides the education and experience table, AWS requires a visual acuity record on its own form showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, and a color perception test. A qualified practitioner must perform it, and AWS limits how old it can be on your examination date. If your experience falls short, the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) carries lower thresholds and lets you work under a CWI while you build your years. The complete table is on the national AWS CWI exam prep page; CWI requirements and career impact covers the rest.

After the CWI: North Jersey career paths

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewal applications due at the third and sixth years and recertification at nine. Locally, inspectors tend to move in a few directions.

  • State special inspector certification alongside the CWI, for those working on buildings.
  • Senior CWI for inspectors who manage inspection programs; see the SCWI pathway.
  • NDT methods for inspectors who want to run tests themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT personnel after training and documented method experience, and Atlantis provides that training: NDT training in Newark, NDT training in New Jersey, VT Level 2 and UT Level 2.

The AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II comparison helps if you are choosing between credentials; Atlantis offers API exam prep separately, as self-paced online courses. For inspection work in the region, see ultrasonic testing in Newark, magnetic particle testing in Newark, penetrant testing in Newark and inspection services in New Jersey. The Practical NDT welding workshop offers browser practice between study sessions.

Nearby CWI pages and a Newark quote

Related CWI exam prep pages: New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington, DC and Buffalo. For how candidates do part by part, see CWI results by exam part.

For a quote, tell us the format, the number of candidates, each person's schooling and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the facility location, the gauges and weld samples on hand and any turnaround or project dates to avoid. Request a Newark CWI exam prep quote; pricing is provided on request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis CWI classroom in Newark?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Newark. You can take the six-day course online at your own pace, as one-to-one sessions with the instructor (online or in person at an agreed location), or as a corporate course at your employer's facility. See the outline.

faq.q: Does passing the CWI make me a New Jersey structural welding special inspector?
faq.a: Not by itself. The DCA's special inspector booklet accepts the AWS CWI examination, or the ICC examination, for the examination step, but you still apply to the Department of Community Affairs and meet its experience or education routes. Check current DCA rules before applying.

The American Welding Society. It reviews your eligibility, runs all three parts of the examination and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates and certifies no one; AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits refinery work in Linden?
faq.a: The ASME option, which combines Section IX welding qualification with the B31.1 power piping and B31.3 process piping codes that refinery piping is built and repaired to.

faq.q: Which code should a bridge or rail steel inspector choose?
faq.a: Usually AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, which bridge owners and many railroad specifications rely on. See AWS D1.5. Inspectors on building steel are usually better served by D1.1.

faq.q: Where do Newark candidates sit the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based, booked at a Prometric center with the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. Part B runs at AWS seminar and examination locations on dates AWS sets, so check the schedule early.

faq.q: Is one-to-one preparation available in person?
faq.a: Yes. The six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor can be held online or in person at a location agreed when you book.

faq.q: Can a special inspection agency have the course delivered for its staff?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format runs the six days at your facility for a group of your inspectors, using your gauges and welds and splitting the code day by book where needed. Request a quote.

faq.q: Are the practice papers made of real AWS questions?
faq.a: No. Every question is original, written by Atlantis to the published AWS topic areas, and Atlantis does not see the live examination.

faq.q: What NDT training can a Newark CWI add?
faq.a: Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; the employer certifies you under its written practice afterwards. See NDT training in Newark.
